text.tspan: 1 · retry at one layer, not every layer
(edge or client owns retries; hops in between fail fast)
clients you don't ship (an editor extension
on laptops you'll never touch)
2 · retry budget + backoff with jitter
(GitHub CTO: retry limits, retry budgets, variable timeouts)
adds no capacity: if first attempts alone are too many,
it only stops you making it worse
3 · defend the server from clients you can't fix
(per-client limits, edge shedding, 403 / 429 + Retry-After)
you're choosing who fails; a buggy client
may ignore the signal anyway
4 · autoscale on the limit you actually hit
(sidecar concurrency, not just the host); alert on saturation
a spike faster than new capacity can start:
that still needs headroom
5 · shrink the shared path
(isolate critical systems, remove shared dependencies)
isolation limits how far one failure spreads,
not whether the first one happens
6 · rehearse the ramp
(site by site; healthy telemetry for N minutes per step)
a gradual ramp is slower by design:
users wait longer, so there's no second wave
